person: Ruth Albers is 63 and has kept the books for her family's thousand-acre corn and soybean farm in central Iowa for forty years. Over the summer she put in eight federal records requests and four county requests about a tile drainage and wetland-determination dispute on their rented-out ground and home tracts. Her son Tyler, who is taking over the field work, expects the paperwork to be kept straight. She does it on her phone at night and distrusts anything that acts on the county office's behalf without telling her. A neighbour once lost a hail claim by missing a deadline, so dates are what she cares about most.
stated_up_front: Tyler and Don want the drainage records for Tract 4417 sorted out before harvest gets going. Can you look at everything we have open with the USDA and the county and tell me which ones need something by what date? And tell me plain what you file for me and what you just get ready.

facts.about: The federal denial that came only by mail
facts.truth: A letter dated 24 July from the NRCS state office denied the request for the wetland-determination file on Tract 4417. It came in the mailbox at the farm office and was scanned into the Drive folder; she never saw it online.
The letter says 90 days, which she counts to Thursday 22 October, and she wants it appealed before then.

facts.about: An older denial the family missed
facts.truth: A denial from the Farm Service Agency county office on the 2023 tile-repair cost-share papers, dated early July. She believes the window already closed on 8 October and that nothing can be done now.

facts.about: The fee dispute with the federal side
facts.truth: An agency requested $1,840 for the contractor's payment records on the Hargrove tile job and labelled the farm a commercial requester. She does not agree the farm is commercial and has not agreed to anything.
The request to the FSA state office in Des Moines went in 30 Aug and was due 30 September. Nothing has come back, and she wants somebody to ask about it.

The Marlow County Supervisors' office billed $584 for drainage district records. Most of it, about $572, is staff time to search and review the records, and only about $12 is for copies. She has not paid.

facts.about: The county request that is late
facts.truth: A county request for the drainage district's meeting minutes went in 24 September and has not been answered. The county sent no letter about it.

Another agency's housing-style FOIA office wrote offering to narrow a broad request for 40 tracts' scores, and wants her answer by 23 October. She would want to talk to Tyler before giving up any tracts.
A company called Requestbright emailed offering to file requests for $249 each. She and Don have always filed their own and she wants it declined.
Her husband is Don and her son is Tyler. They want to see anything before it goes out under the farm's name, 'Albers Farms'.

unknowns: Whether a request that is simply late can be appealed, or whether she has to wait for an answer first
What exactly 'commercial-use' means as a fee category and whether the farm fits it
Whether the county can charge for staff time and whether there is anyone above the county to appeal to
How many working days an agency really has to answer, and which holidays count
